transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Um… mainly work stuff. I keep getting up from my desk during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing claims. It’s been… hard to manage.
Do you get distracted easily while you’re trying to work?

Yeah… pretty easily. If people near me start talking about another claim, or I suddenly remember some random errand, I kind of lose the thread of what I’m reading. Then I have to go back and reread the same part a few times.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t totally new. In elementary school, teachers would write stuff like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets or miss instructions. I needed reminders to actually finish classwork sometimes.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?
Not really, no. I mean, I’ve had nights where I stayed up too late, but not like… feeling unusually energized and not needing sleep.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?
Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I get distracted or things come to mind, but not like unwanted thoughts I can’t shake.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to stay seated when you’re expected to?
Yeah… that’s actually kind of the main thing. At work I keep getting up from my workstation, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish the claim reviews. It’s… been hard to stay put.
Do you have the same trouble sitting still and staying focused in other settings, like at home?

Yeah… mostly at work is where it’s been obvious. I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish the claim reviews. At home, I guess I’m not paying attention to it as much.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
I don’t think so… I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, but not like it’s always there for no reason.
Outside of work, do these attention or restlessness problems ever cause trouble for you?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it causing much trouble outside work… or I guess I don’t pay as much attention to it there.
Have these attention or restlessness problems ever caused trouble for you in relationships?
Not really… I mean, I can’t think of anything specific. Maybe people get annoyed sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it causing relationship problems.
Did these problems start after a particularly stressful event at work or in your life?

No, I don’t think it started after one specific stressful thing. Looking back, it was kind of there when I was a kid too. Teachers would say I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets or miss instructions and needed reminders to finish classwork.
At home, do you often have trouble finishing everyday tasks?
I’m not sure. I mean, I do the usual stuff at home, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s a pattern or anything.
At home, do you often leave chores or household tasks unfinished?
I don’t know… sometimes, maybe. I’ll start something and then come back to it later, but I’m not sure if I’d say it’s often.
At home, do these attention or restlessness problems make it hard for you to manage things the way you want to?

Yeah… I guess it does, especially with work. My supervisor put me on performance coaching because my claim files are falling behind, and they’ve been questioning my accuracy. I’m trying not to make a big deal of it, but I’m worried it could mess up the senior adjuster track I was hoping for.
When you were a child, were you often fidgety or unable to stay seated when you were expected to?

I don’t really remember being fidgety or out of my seat that much. What I do remember is teachers saying I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, and need reminders to finish classwork. So… it wasn’t exactly new, I guess.
Do you often feel driven to keep moving, like it’s hard to relax even when you want to?
Not really, no. I mean, I can feel restless sometimes, but I don’t usually feel like I have to keep moving or anything like that.
As a child, did you often blurt out answers or interrupt other people before they were finished?
I don’t think so. I mean, maybe once in a while like any kid, but I don’t remember that being something teachers or my parents complained about.
As a child, did your trouble paying attention happen at home too, or mainly at school?

I remember it more from school, honestly. Teachers would write that I was bright but losing worksheets, missing instructions, needing reminders to finish classwork… stuff like that. At home, I’m less sure.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet when you’re sitting?
Yeah, I do some. In longer meetings or trainings, I’ll catch myself bouncing my leg or clicking a pen, or just shifting around in the chair. I try not to make it obvious.
Do you often interrupt other people when they’re talking?
Not really, no. I mean, I might jump in sometimes if I’m worried I’ll forget what I was going to say, but I don’t think people would describe me as interrupting a lot.
